groups.label: Basic Word Order (SVO)
groups.definition: Canonical Subject-Verb-Object English sentence structure and adverb placement.
rules: Standard order: Subject + Verb + Direct Object + Manner + Place + Time.
Frequency Adverbs: Place before main verbs, but AFTER verb to be (I always eat breakfast / She is never late).

examples.t: She speaks English fluently at work.

groups.label: There is / There are
groups.definition: Existential structures asserting the presence or existence of singular/uncountable or plural entities.
rules: There is + singular countable or uncountable noun (There is a book / There is water).
There are + plural countable noun (There are three apples).

examples.t: There is a book on the table.
There are three people in the room.

groups.label: Theme/Rheme Information Packaging
groups.definition: Strategic discourse alignment placing known context at sentence start (Theme) and new heavy information at sentence end (Rheme / End-Weight).
rules: Place established context in Theme position at the beginning of the sentence.
Place new, crucial, or heavy information in Rheme position at the end of the sentence.

examples.t: Underpinning the recovery plan was an uncompromising commitment to environmental policy.
